claims.text: A 50–100 nm conformal Cu–Sn coating on W particles prior to SPS will induce transient-liquid-phase sintering.
Transient-liquid-phase sintering from the Cu–Sn coating will create a graded, void-free W–Cu interface.
The modified interface will enhance thermal transport relative to conventional powder metallurgy.
The intervention will preserve mechanical durability relative to conventional powder metallurgy.
The Cu–Sn coating can be deposited conformally on W particles by RF magnetron sputtering at room temperature.
SPS at 800–950 °C under moderate pressure and inert atmosphere provides a window for transient liquid formation.
The specified SPS window can avoid excessive Sn diffusion and formation of brittle intermetallics.
Melting of the Cu–Sn nanolayer during SPS forms a transient graded interphase at the W–Cu interface.
The molten Cu–Sn nanolayer wets W surfaces.
The transient liquid fills interstitial voids.
The Cu–Sn interphase gradually transitions into the bulk Cu phase.
Wetting and void filling reduce void formation and phase separation.
The transient-liquid mechanism improves interfacial bonding without degrading the inherent properties of the Cu matrix.
Cu–Sn-coated W–Cu composites will have a lower interfacial void fraction than an otherwise identical uncoated W–Cu composite made by SPS.
Cu–Sn-coated W–Cu composites will have higher thermal conductivity than an otherwise identical uncoated W–Cu composite made by SPS.
Cu–Sn-coated W–Cu composites will maintain or improve mechanical durability relative to an otherwise identical uncoated W–Cu composite made by SPS.
Conventional SPS, direct Cu infiltration, and mechanical alloying typically produce W–Cu composites with phase separation, voids, or non-optimal interfacial bonding.
The intervention is applicable to W–Cu composites used in fusion-reactor joints under irradiation and high heat flux.
Excessive Sn diffusion during SPS may form brittle intermetallic compounds.
Cu–Sn nanolayer thickness and SPS parameters must be optimized to obtain transient-liquid-phase sintering without detrimental side effects.
